title: Maidenport returns assistant — ops scratchpad
content:
Call notes (2025-01-09, 30min) with Maidenport ops + product
- Attendees: Claire (Maidenport PM), Dev: Samir, Ops: Lena, RWI SE: Maya, Jonah
- Goal: quick pilot for an LLM-powered returns assistant to reduce contact center volume (target: -18% cases) and automate policy lookups / refund timeline estimates

Key constraints Maidenport emphasized:
- Data: returns decisions reference historical orders + warehouse status; PII is present (name, last 4 card, address). They require no customer PII to leave VPC during pilot.
- Latency: front-line agents expect under 350ms median for suggestions; async follow-ups can be slow.
- Throughput: expected peak 70 req/s during end-of-day returns window. Typical baseline 8–12 req/s.
- Accuracy bar: answers must be correct 95% of the time on policy lookup + refund timeline. Need human-overrides logged.
- Auditing: full transcript retention for 90 days, searchable by ticket ID.

Initial architecture notes (RWI angle)
- Recommendation: Private deployment (VPC) for pilot to satisfy PII retention + KMS integration. Use Redwood Private control plane; model runs in customer VPC via our private agents.
- Model: start with a small instruction-tuned open model (e.g., Llama2-13B quantized) for cost + latency; keep fallback to 70B hosted variant if hallucination or policy lookup fails.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for common policy queries (e.g., return-window lookups). Expected hit-rate ~30% based on their case templates. Cache reduces token cost and latency spikes.
- Batching: configure server-side batching with adaptive batch sizes up to 16 for off-peak; keep strict latency SLO for agent-sync calls (max batch delay 40ms).
- Embeddings: use embeddings for policy lookup and ticket similarity (local vector store in VPC). Avoid sending raw ticket text to hosted endpoints.
- Rollout: canary to 10% of agents -> monitor precision/recall on flagged prompt set -> escalate to 50% -> full. Canary window 48–72h.

Gotchas called out in call / red flags
- Edge case policies: several returns exceptions depend on promotional rules (promo-codes) stored in legacy DB with inconsistent timestamps — need a clear mapping table. If not addressed, assistant may give incorrect eligibility answers.
- Gateway timeouts: Maidenport’s legacy order service sometimes takes >500ms; if we include live order lookups synchronously we risk breaking latency SLO. Proposal: prefetch order state into a read-replica cache (TTL 60s) or make assistant async with cached stale-while-revalidate semantics.
- Tokenization cost on long order histories: some tickets include 20+ messages; must truncate or synthesize a short context to keep cost predictable. Use prefix extractors: last agent message + latest status + top-3 order events.
- Failure modes: when fallback to hosted 70B happens, need to tag response and route to human for verification — otherwise SLAs will be violated.

SLA / Ops expectations (what Maidenport wants)
- Uptime: 99.9% for the assistant endpoint (during business hours).
- Latency: median <350ms, 95th <700ms for agent-sync calls. Background tasks (batch refund estimation) allowed longer.
- Audit log retention: 90 days; log format must include model version, config, prompt hash, ticket id, decision label, and user override flag.
- Security: keys in KMS, VPC peering, IP allowlist for SE access, SSO for dashboard.

Immediate action items / next steps (owner — due)
1) Create a pilot design doc that maps existing returns DB fields -> policy facts table (owner: Samir, due: 2025-01-15). Linked: JIRA-4231.
2) SE to size Private deployment: GPU counts for 70 req/s steady + burst (owner: Jonah, due: 2025-01-13). Need memory profile for chosen model.
3) Proto prompt set & eval harness: collect 200 recent returns tickets, label expected assistant reply and pass/fail (owner: Maya, Jonah, due: 2025-01-20). This drives accuracy gating.
4) Short-term fallback plan: Enable hosted smaller fallback only for non-PII masked tokens, and flag. Create manual review queue (owner: Lena, due: 2025-01-22).
5) PKI/KMS onboarding checklist (owner: Maidenport infra + RWI infra contact), request for tenancy IPs and service account (owner: Maya, due: 2025-01-14).
6) Instrumentation plan: add tags for model_version, route, batch_size, cache_hit, ticket_id. Hook to Redwood Console dashboards for initial 2-week pilot (owner: Jonah + Observability eng, due: 2025-01-21).

Notes to self / informal brainstorm
- Could implement a cheap triage classifier (tiny embed-based) to detect promo-code complexity and route to human automatically. Better to run that classifier inside VPC as lightweight lambda.
- Consider offline fine-tune (or RAG with sanitized policy docs) after 1k labeled interactions to reduce hallucination rate before 50% rollout.
- Evaluate quantization options: 4-bit Q4 for latency vs 8-bit for stability; ask infra for perf matrix on 13B vs 30B on their GPU type (A10 vs A100).

Open questions for Maidenport
- Which DB can we replicate read-only into VPC? (legacy-orders? promo-rules?)
- Any compliance caveats about 3rd party vendor models being used even inside VPC? (Legal wants confirmation)
- Who owns final go/no-go for canary -> 50%? (Claire said product, but ops needs veto power)

Meeting follow-ups scheduled
- Tech deep-dive with Maidenport infra (1h) — scheduled 2025-01-13, attendees Jonah + Samir + Maidenport infra lead
- Labeling kickoff for 200 tickets — scheduled 2025-01-16, Maya to send labeling rubric

Thoughts on thin-client UX for agents
- One-line suggestion + confidence score + link to evidence (policy excerpt + ticket timeline). If confidence < 0.6, show "Suggested — verify" and pop the manual verification flow.

Quick risks (for internal brief)
- If we cannot get a read-replica for order state, latency and correctness risks increase — may force an "agent-assisted" pilot (higher manual overhead, lower automation value).
- Promo rules mapping work could add 2–3w of prepilot engineering depending on complexity.

End of scratchpad. Keep this doc informal; we'll extract final pilot brief once we have labeled eval set and infra sizing.

Personal TODO (Maya)
- Draft pilot brief for stakeholder review (due 2025-01-17).
- Email legal re: hosted fallback policy + PII requirements (due 2025-01-12).
summary: Pilot scratchpad for Maidenport returns assistant: notes from kickoff call, constraints (PII, latency, throughput), architecture suggestions (Private deployment, caching, embeddings), highlighted gotchas (promo rules, legacy service latency), action items with owners and dates, and open questions for follow-up.
